solutions.check: 26 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: A minute implant in boob operation, which grows quickly

definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing for the plant

indicators.note: an implant is put inside something, so these letters go inside the next word
an operation works on the body and changes it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for minute
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tiny implant is put in during a breast operation, and things grow fast afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: A and M go inside BOOB, then the whole lot is rearranged. Private Eye surfaces are often deliberately cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: This giant grass is famous as one of the fastest growing plants on earth, adding many centimetres per day.

clue.text: God, Spike's having core of penis removed!

indicators.note: the core is the very centre, so only the middle letter of the following word is wanted
something removed is taken away, so that letter comes out of the longer word

blocks.note: a thorn is a sharp spike on a plant
the third of its five letters

explanation.surface: An exclamation of horror about someone called Spike undergoing a very painful operation.
explanation.walkthrough: THORN loses its N to leave THOR. 'Spike's' reads as a man's name with a possessive, but it is a common noun plus 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thor is the Norse deity of thunder who wields a hammer, so he is one of the gods.

clue.text: Sucker may tease outrageously

indicators.note: behaving outrageously means acting wildly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A gullible person might find themselves teased mercilessly.
explanation.definitionFit: A sucker is a gullible person who is an easy target, and that idiom describes someone readily exploited or beaten.

clue.text: Like more power (official), Brenda?

blocks.note: P is the symbol for power
a referee is a sports official
Brenda is Private Eye's long-running nickname for Queen Elizabeth II, whose cipher is ER

explanation.surface: A question to the Queen: would she prefer more official power?
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye calls the late Queen 'Brenda'; ER stands for Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: To favour one option over another is to like it better, a straightforward synonym for the verb.

clue.text: A dire Bush, embracing Republican leader, abandoned and taken out of the picture?

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter of the party name is used
to embrace is to hold inside one's arms, so the earlier letters surround the next piece
abandoned can mean wild and unrestrained, so the letters are freely rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A terrible President Bush, hugging his party leader, is ditched and quietly erased from the photo.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the end phrase, with its question mark marking a playful sense: an airbrush can remove a person from a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: Airbrushing a photo retouches it, and politicians fallen from favour have notoriously been edited out of official images that way.

clue.text: Wind's a prominent feature with nothing on, all right

blocks.note: a chin is a facial feature that can be prominent
zero, shaped like the letter O
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Someone notes that wind is an obvious feature when you wear nothing, and that's fine.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinook is a warm dry wind that blows down the eastern slopes of the Rocky Mountains.

clue.text: Explosive end when not prepared to back the crown

indicators.note: to go back is to travel the other way, so the word for unprepared is read right to left

blocks.note: raw food has not been prepared or cooked
the crown is the top of the head

explanation.surface: A dramatic ending comes when people are unwilling to support the monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface 'back' means support the crown, but cryptically it is the turnaround signal acting on the word for unprepared.
explanation.definitionFit: The front section of a missile carrying the bomb is the explosive tip of the weapon.

clue.text: A load of creeps taking drug

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it within, so the drug letter goes inside

blocks.note: the creeps is a feeling of fright
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A gang of unpleasant people are all on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A load of' reads as 'a lot of', but 'A load' is the definition; 'creeps' is a noun meaning a sense of dread.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods carried by lorry, ship or plane form a cargo, which is a load being transported.

clue.text: Clegg, ultimately an apprentice, dishing out the campaigning politician's effusive welcome

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter of the name is kept

blocks.note: last letter of the name
a lad is a youngster learning a trade, as an apprentice is
to dish out is to hand out

explanation.surface: Nick Clegg, a novice at the end, hands out the kind of over-the-top greeting politicians give on the campaign trail.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Clegg was the Liberal Democrat leader and Deputy Prime Minister in the 2010 coalition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaking hands warmly and enthusiastically with everyone, often insincerely, is what candidates do when canvassing for votes.

clue.text: (& 23dn.) England fans need somewhere to booze and ... well, a host

blocks.note: a bar is a place to drink
'my!' and 'well!' are both exclamations of surprise
a host is an army or great multitude

explanation.surface: England supporters need a pub to drink in and, well, someone to put them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' looks like a landlord, but here it is the old sense of a large army.
explanation.definitionFit: The travelling supporters of England's cricket team are famously known by this nickname, celebrating their noisy loyalty.

clue.text: Arty side of European capital's archaic, sinister financial institution

blocks.note: sinister is Latin for left, a sense now archaic outside heraldry
a bank is a financial institution

explanation.surface: A sinister old bank sits in the artistic quarter of a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sinister' in the surface means menacing, but its old meaning is left-hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The south side of the Seine in Paris is historically associated with artists, writers and bohemian intellectuals.

clue.text: Something missed by the like of Salmond's cheap marketing ploy?

blocks.note: a loss is something you miss once it has gone
Alex Salmond was leader of the Scottish National Party

explanation.surface: A dig at Alex Salmond, whose referendum campaign is cast as a cheap marketing gimmick.
explanation.walkthrough: Salmond led the SNP and the Yes side in the 2014 Scottish independence referendum, lost it, and resigned, so he was literally a leader with a loss.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops sell an item below cost to draw customers in, hoping they buy other profitable goods.

clue.text: Alternative chosen mode which is taken advantage of by many a Westminster MP

definitions.text: which is taken advantage of by many a Westminster MP
definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing for a noun

indicators.note: an alternative is a different version, so the letters are arranged another way

blocks.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A remark on a favoured lifestyle that many MPs exploit.
explanation.walkthrough: In the 2009 expenses scandal many MPs claimed public money for a London or constituency property, so the definition is a satirical one.
explanation.definitionFit: MPs could claim allowances for an extra property, and many were found to be exploiting that rule for profit.

clue.text: see 18ac.
(& 22ac.) Well, maybe not so plucky having voted for the status quo patriotic hymn

blocks.clueFragment: Well, maybe not so plucky having voted for the status quo
blocks.note: surface reading: someone has lost their nerve and stuck with what they had
setter's reading: the unofficial anthem of a nation whose name and courage are in the title, which in 2014 voted to stay in the UK

explanation.surface: A sardonic note that a supposedly courageous nation chickened out at the ballot box.
explanation.walkthrough: In the 2014 independence referendum Scotland voted No and stayed in the UK, so the setter teases that the brave song title no longer quite fits.
explanation.definitionFit: This rousing song serves as an unofficial national anthem, sung at sporting events and on patriotic occasions.

clue.text: Boxers getting stiff?  That's a fag

blocks.note: boxers are a breed of dog
a stiff is slang for a corpse

explanation.surface: Boxing fighters getting stiff muscles before someone lights a cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: In British public schools a fag was a junior boy who did chores for an older pupil; a dogsbody is a drudge doing menial work.
explanation.definitionFit: A fag is British slang for a drudge or menial servant, as is the person who does all the tedious jobs.

clue.text: Domingo's sounding tender?

indicators.note: sounding means as heard in speech, so the word is taken by its pronunciation

blocks.note: Placido Domingo was one of the Three Tenors, so he and his kind are tenors

explanation.surface: Is the opera singer Placido Domingo singing softly and lovingly?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like an adjective about a gentle voice, but it is the noun for money, as in legal tender; a tenner is a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten-pound notes are banknotes, which are legal tender, so they serve as an example of currency.

clue.text: (& 14ac.) Blair's 'issue' a flipping joke at heart – name added to apply pressure

indicators.note: to flip something is to turn it over, so the word for a joke is read backwards
something at the heart sits in the middle, so these letters go inside the name
added means put on the end, so the abbreviation follows everything else

blocks.note: Leo is the youngest son of Tony Blair, born while he was Prime Minister
taken as written
a pun is a joke on words
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Tony Blair's problem looks like a bad joke, and naming someone becomes a way to apply pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' is in quotes because it means offspring, not a political problem. A and the joke turned round sit inside Blair's son's name, then N goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To pressurise or coerce someone is to bear heavily on them, an informal phrasal verb for intimidation.

clue.text: Pop star, no range, a round prima donna who once had a modestly long hairy ride

definitions.text: who once had a modestly long hairy ride
definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing for a person

indicators.note: no means without, so the cooker brand is taken out of the singer's name

blocks.note: Lady Gaga is an American pop singer
an Aga is a British brand of range cooker
a round shape looks like the letter O
a diva is a prima donna

explanation.surface: A pop star without a vocal range turns diva, compared with someone famous for a naked horse ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' looks like a singer's vocal range, but it is a kitchen stove; removing AGA from the singer leaves LADYG.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says this Anglo-Saxon noblewoman rode naked through Coventry covered only by her long hair, protesting her husband's taxes.

clue.text: Silliness of live broadcast – politician has no alternative

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, as seed is, so the letters are spread into a new order
having none of something means it is missing, so those letters are dropped from the politician

blocks.note: taken as written
a Tory is a British Conservative politician
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A complaint about the absurdity of live TV, where a politician is left with no choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live broadcast' reads as one phrase, but 'broadcast' rearranges LIVE; the Tory without OR leaves TY.
explanation.definitionFit: Levity is light-heartedness and lack of seriousness, which is a close synonym of frivolous foolishness.

clue.text: Capital backing for old queen (fourth)

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the whole phrase is read from the end

blocks.note: Queen Anne reigned in the early 1700s
IV is the Roman numeral four, as in a regnal number

explanation.surface: Money is raised to support an elderly queen, the fourth of her name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital backing' looks like financial support, but Capital is the definition and 'backing' reverses ANNE IV.
explanation.definitionFit: Vienna is the capital city of Austria, so it fits a simple capital city definition.

clue.text: Sun forced to entertain its own end, which is a bit hairy

indicators.note: forced means pushed out of shape, so these letters are bent into a new order
its own end points back to the first word and takes its last letter

blocks.note: the three letters rearranged
to have guests is to entertain them
the last letter of the opening word

explanation.surface: The Sun newspaper is made to cover itself, and the result is a little risqué.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit hairy' sounds like 'a bit risky', but it means stubbly.
explanation.definitionFit: A face that has not been shaved has stubble, so it is somewhat hairy.

clue.text: see 15ac.
see 10ac.
Upgrade old hooker adding speck of dust

blocks.note: pro is slang for a prostitute
a mote is a tiny speck, as of dust

explanation.surface: Instructions to smarten up an elderly prostitute by adding a little dirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooker' might suggest a rugby position, but it is slang for a sex worker.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise someone to a higher rank or position is to give them a step up in status.

clue.text: Unpaired blokes having time for a bit on the side?

blocks.note: an odd sock has no partner
blokes is British slang for men
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Single men making time for an extramarital affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit on the side' usually means a lover, but here it is literally a leftover scrap set aside.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddment is a leftover remnant or scrap, the sort of spare fragment put aside after the rest is used.
